elements.element: Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.
elements.evidence: The rendered Section 10.3(A) deletes the all-requirements covenant ("Customer shall be required to obtain from M&I all of those Services which are included in the Monthly Base Fee") and substitutes: "M&I shall be a non-exclusive provider of the Services, and Customer shall have no obligation to obtain any Services exclusively from M&I." No retained sentence imposes a sourcing, requirements, or sole-supplier duty; the surviving first sentence is only a pricing acknowledgment. The rationale confirms the other "exclusive" references run in Customer's favour or are unrelated (Sections 21.10, 21.11 are scope/pricing assumptions; Section 1.1(C) is a recital).

elements.element: Exclusivity is limited to a defined product category.
elements.evidence: Condition inapplicable: after the edit there is no exclusivity commitment on Customer at all (M&I is expressly a "non-exclusive provider"), so there is no exclusive scope that could exceed a defined product category.

elements.element: Exclusivity lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Condition inapplicable: the eight-year "during the Term" sourcing obligation is deleted and no exclusivity of any duration remains, so no period can exceed 12 months.

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet service levels.
elements.evidence: Condition inapplicable: with no exclusivity in force, no performance-based release from exclusivity is required; Customer is free at all times to source elsewhere regardless of M&I's Article 9 Performance Standards.

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet delivery dates.
elements.evidence: Condition inapplicable: no exclusivity or delivery-date-linked lock-in survives the edit, so Customer's alternative-sourcing freedom is unconditional.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the single operative sentence creating the requirements obligation is replaced with an unconditional non-exclusivity statement, and no residual sourcing covenant, right-to-match, or prohibition on third-party procurement remains.

Minimality holds: only the offending second sentence of Section 10.3(A) was touched. The favourable/neutral pricing acknowledgment in the first sentence is retained verbatim, and the inserted language adds no obligation outside the checklist (no survival tail, no remedies, no procedure, no cap or category/duration mechanics that would be needed only at the fallback). The affirmative "non-exclusive provider" phrasing is a permissible concise replacement for a deleted covenant rather than an extra requirement.

Intent preserved: the deleted "as set forth on Schedule 6.2" cross-reference travelled with the deleted covenant and Schedule 6.2 remains operative for pricing elsewhere; the retained first sentence (pricing based on Integrated Banking System services) does not contradict non-exclusivity, and no undefined term or dangling reference is created.

Fallback elements are recorded as vacuously met because the redline eliminates exclusivity entirely; the drafter should not add category/12-month/performance-exit language, which would be non-minimal at the preferred level.

Note for negotiation only (not an operative gap): the margin comment correctly reserves the fallback (defined category, 12 months, automatic release on Performance Standard or delivery-date failure) as a talking point without importing it into the text.
